what_you_do: Take Saturday STEM classes at MIT during the school year, from robotics to bioengineering, in a multi-year program with college application guidance. Lunch is free.
pay_detail: Free of charge. Students pay only their own transportation to MIT (Lawrence students get free transport).
duration: 8 Saturdays in spring and 8 in fall, 10:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., for up to about five and a half years
deadline_text: The application deadline is not stated on the program pages read. Check the Apply page.

name: MITES Summer
org: MIT (MITES, Introduction to Technology, Engineering and Science)
what_you_do: Spend six weeks on the MIT campus taking five math, science and humanities courses, touring labs and companies, and getting college admissions counseling. Room and board are free.
grades: 11th grade at time of application (rising seniors)
pay_detail: Free of charge. Students pay only for transportation; travel scholarships are available for MITES Summer.
duration: Six weeks, late June through early August, weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
deadline_text: The application deadline is not stated on the pages read. Check the Apply page.

name: Summer Teen Internship Program
what_you_do: Work as a Visitor Services Assistant or an Aquarium Guide, greeting visitors and explaining exhibits and ocean conservation, with training in marine science, climate science and public speaking.
pay_detail: All teen internships are paid positions (rate not stated)
duration: One week of training and six weeks of work
deadline_text: The summer 2026 application is closed. The page says to check back next March for the summer 2027 application.

name: Librarians of Tomorrow
what_you_do: Teen internship in library careers: training and field trips on library, college and career skills, then hands-on work helping with programs and welcoming visitors, plus a capstone project. About 100 hours total.
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated), plus volunteer service hours.
duration: Nov 2026 to June 2027, 3-6 hours a week, 100 hours total
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application deadline was October 3, 2026. Expect the next call in fall 2027 (last-year pattern).

name: StoryTeen
what_you_do: Teen internship in early literacy and early childhood education: training on child development and literacy, helping children's librarians with storytimes and events, and a creative project. About 100 hours total.
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated), plus volunteer service hours.
duration: Nov 2026 to May 2027, 3-5 hours a week, 100 hours total
deadline_text: Applications for 2026-27 were open through October 3, 2026. Expect the next call in fall 2027 (last-year pattern).

name: Teen Night Out Branch Council
what_you_do: Interns plan, promote and host after-hours library programs for other teens. You learn event planning, budgeting and promotion, meet weekly as a team, and give teens a voice in library decisions.
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated), plus volunteer service hours.
duration: Weekly meetings Oct 2026 to June 2027, 75 hours of service
deadline_text: Applications for 2026-27 were open through October 3, 2026. Expect the next call in fall 2027 (last-year pattern).

name: Teaching Intern and Summer Volunteer
what_you_do: Teach and tutor middle schoolers in a six-week summer program after 80 hours of training. The site says college and high school students serve as teachers.
pay_detail: Pay not stated. Ask the program.
duration: 6-week summer program
deadline_text: Not posted.

name: Volunteer program
what_you_do: Welcome visitors as a podium attendant, gallery roamer, school group volunteer or programs and events helper at the state history museum.
pay_detail: Unpaid. After 25 hours of service volunteers can get a complimentary museum membership.
duration: At least 6 hours per month
deadline_text: The page says applications for the volunteer program are open. No deadline is stated.

name: American Legion California Boys State (Boys & Girls State)
what_you_do: You spend a week at Sacramento State in a summer program for students who finished junior year. You run a mock state government. It has been open to all genders since 2023.
grades: Finished 11th grade, with at least one semester of high school left
pay_detail: Registration fee listed as $550 per delegate on the Key Dates page (the page does not label the year). Ask your sponsoring Post who pays.
duration: One week in June at Sacramento State. The site counts down to June 19, 2027.
deadline_text: 2027 selection dates are not posted. The Key Dates page (year not labeled) shows delegate selection Jan 15 to Apr 1 and all registrations due Apr 1. Posts usually interview late Jan to late March.

name: California Highway Patrol Explorer Program
what_you_do: Teens in Explorer posts train in law enforcement skills and can compete at the CHP statewide Explorer competition, held at the CHP Academy in West Sacramento. Contact CHP to find a post.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cost to you: 2026 competition fees were $150 per explorer, $125 per advisor and $75 per spectator.
duration: Not stated for post membership. The 2026 competition ran April 24 to 26, 2026.
deadline_text: No post sign-up dates are stated. The 2026 competition registration opened December 2025 and full payment was due February 23, 2026. Both have passed.

name: California Division of Apprenticeship Standards: how apprenticeship works and minimum ages
org: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Apprenticeship Standards
what_you_do: You can use the Apprenticeship Search to find registered apprenticeship and pre-apprenticeship programs near you. The state agency that registers them is the Division of Apprenticeship Standards.
pay_detail: DAS describes apprenticeship as earn-and-learn. Wages depend on the program; DAS has a tool to look up apprenticeship wages.
deadline_text: Each program sets its own application window.

name: California State Parks Volunteers in Parks (youth)
what_you_do: You can volunteer or intern at state parks. If you are under 18, you can volunteer with written permission from a parent or guardian.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Varies by park
deadline_text: Rolling.

name: California Work Experience Education (Exploratory, General, Career Technical)
what_you_do: Work Experience Education (WEE) is a school-supervised job that earns class credit. Exploratory WEE is unpaid job sampling and can start at age 12. General and Career Technical WEE are paid jobs that come with a related class.
pay_detail: Exploratory is unpaid. General and Career Technical WEE combine paid work with a class.
deadline_text: Ask your counselor or the school's work experience coordinator.

name: Next-Gen Manufacturing Academy (High School Summer Academy)
what_you_do: Summer days on campus building skills in engineering, robotics and AI, including smart robots. No experience needed.
pay_detail: $25 per person. Parking permit and daily lunch included.
duration: Held each July, daily 9:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., at Cal Poly Pomona Building 17
deadline_text: Page says applications open in January and close in April each year. Exact 2027 dates not posted.

name: California 4-H Youth Development
what_you_do: You can join youth clubs and projects in science, agriculture, leadership and community service. Teen leader roles are also available.
pay_detail: Not confirmed. Fees depend on the county program.
duration: Club year
deadline_text: Join through a county 4-H program.

name: California FFA and Supervised Agricultural Experience (SAE)
org: California FFA and National FFA Organization
what_you_do: Learn agriculture in class, run a hands-on Supervised Agricultural Experience (a job or project), and build leadership through events.
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the pages read. Ask your ag teacher what your chapter charges.
duration: School year; SAE can be year-round
deadline_text: Join through your ag teacher.

name: California Partnership Academies (CPA)
what_you_do: You can join a three-year 'school within a school' for grades 10 to 12. It mixes academics with a career focus, business mentors and internships.
pay_detail: The CDE page does not say whether internships pay or give school credit. Ask the school.
duration: 3 years
deadline_text: The CDE page lists no student application dates. Each school sets its own.

name: Capital Area NextGen Youth Services
org: Capital Area Workforce Development Board (NCWorks Career Centers)
what_you_do: Youth specialists help young job seekers with tutoring, career exploration, entry-level job training and mock interviews.
pay_detail: Apprenticeships and work experience are listed as services. Whether work experience is paid is not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: The page does not state a deadline or enrollment status. Use the Complete an Interest Form button.

name: College Preview (pre-college art and design program)
what_you_do: Spend two weeks on campus taking college-level classes in an art or design major, earn college credit, build a portfolio and show work in a gallery exhibition.
pay_detail: Commuter $3,000 total ($2,750 tuition and fees plus a $250 registration fee). Residential $3,600 total (adds $600 room and board). Scholarships available.
duration: 2 weeks (2026: July 12 to 25)
deadline_text: 2026 session: registration opened Nov 3, 2025, scholarship applications closed April 27, 2026, registration closed May 11, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Supporting Student Success (WIOA In-School Youth)
org: Contra Costa County Office of Education
city: Contra Costa County, CA (West County and East County)
what_you_do: If you are a high school student who qualifies, you get a case manager, career exploration, and paid job training and work experience.
pay_detail: Paid workforce prep and work experience (rate not posted)
deadline_text: Ongoing

name: Cedars-Sinai Teen Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Help at a large hospital by scanning and entering data, welcoming new patients, answering phones, and delivering flowers and amenities. Teens do not do research or assist with medical procedures.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers buy the required volunteer jacket for $30 (cash) and wear black or white scrubs.
duration: Winter/Spring and Fall: one 2-hour shift a week for 10 weeks (20 hours). Summer: two 4-hour shifts a week for 5 weeks (40 hours).
deadline_text: 2027 sessions: Winter/Spring (Jan 25 to Apr 4) applications Nov 23, 2026; Summer (Jun 21 to Jul 25) applications Mar 29, 2027; Fall (Oct 4 to Dec 12) applications Aug 2, 2027. First come, first served; each application closes when spots fill.

name: Chabot College Early College (Dual Enrollment)
what_you_do: Tuition-free college classes while you are in high school. You can take individual classes at Chabot College or online, take college classes offered at your own high school, or attend a summer academy.
pay_detail: Enrollment fees are waived. Out-of-state and international students pay $370 per unit. You buy your own books and arrange your own transportation. Maximum 11 units.
duration: Per term
deadline_text: Rolling by term.

name: Galaxy Explorers Program
what_you_do: You spend three years in this STEM and workforce program. You work museum floor shifts explaining science, join inquiry teams on engineering and tech projects, and can take leadership roles in later years.
grades: Typically enters the summer before 10th grade and stays through 12th grade
pay_detail: Annual tuition is $1,500 per student (one payment by June 1, or $750 by June 1 and $750 by September 1). The need-based Career Access program covers tuition and adds a stipend. 12th-grade Interns receive a stipend.
duration: 3 years (summer before 10th grade through 12th grade)
deadline_text: Applications open each year from February 1 to March 31. Decisions in early May, orientation early to mid June. The page does not list 2027 dates.

name: Carle Foundation Hospital Student Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Volunteer at Carle Foundation Hospital as a high school or college student. The program has about 500 students each semester.
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: By term (fall, spring, summer)
deadline_text: Applications are due by 5 p.m. on August 29 (fall term), November 15 (spring term) or April 15 (summer term). The page gives no year.

name: Youth Services (Workforce Development)
what_you_do: Career planning, job search help, resume and interview practice, and work experience for young people, at the Champaign County workNet center.
pay_detail: Not stated for youth. A separate Work Experience page says qualified interns can have up to 240 hours of wages covered.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: None stated on the page.

name: Counselor-in-Training, Summer Day Camps
what_you_do: Volunteer as a counselor-in-training at summer day camps at Homer Lake and Lake of the Woods forest preserves.
pay_detail: Volunteer position.
duration: Summer day camps (June to July per the volunteer page); weekly hours not stated
deadline_text: No application dates posted.

name: Champaign Park District Seasonal and Summer Jobs
what_you_do: Seasonal park district jobs: lifeguard and swim instructor at Sholem Aquatic Center, summer camp staff, Prairie Farm, sports and grounds positions.
pay_detail: Not stated on the pages read. Lifeguard certification is covered 100% by the Park District.
duration: Seasonal jobs run April to November and do not exceed 6 months; summer camp is a 10-week program
deadline_text: No application dates or deadlines listed on the page.

name: Champaign Park District Teen Volunteering
what_you_do: Volunteer at parks and programs such as special events, Prairie Farm (May to August), Virginia Theatre, sports and summer programs.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Hours can count toward high school volunteer requirements.
duration: Varies by role
deadline_text: No deadline. Volunteers register on the Champaign Park District Volunteer Portal.

name: Dual Credit and Dual Enrollment at Parkland College
what_you_do: Take Parkland College classes while in high school (on campus, online or at your high school) and earn college credit, and in some cases high school credit too.
pay_detail: Tuition is not stated on this page. It says courses are affordable and in some cases reduced or tuition-free.
duration: By semester
deadline_text: No deadline on the page. Ask the Early College office.

name: Champaign Public Library Volunteers
what_you_do: Help the library with sorting and shelving, bookstore cashier shifts, storytime help, a summer Club Fred program and other listed roles. Training is provided.
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: Typically 2 to 3 hours a week; a 4-month minimum is preferred
deadline_text: No deadline.

grades: Rising 7th to 12th grade. Individual camps have narrower ranges, such as 7th to 9th or 10th to 12th.
name: Grainger Engineering Summer Camps
what_you_do: Week-long camps with hands-on projects, lab tours and classes from Illinois engineering faculty and students, in areas such as aerospace, bioengineering, electronics and AI, and quantum.
pay_detail: 2026 prices: residential $1,500, commuter $750, day camp $550, each plus a $25 deposit. The Trail Blazer Scholarship covers 50% or 100% for students who meet its criteria.
duration: One week per camp (June to August in 2026)
deadline_text: All 2026 camps are listed as full. 2027 application dates are not posted.

name: Young Scholars STEMM Research Program
what_you_do: Six weeks of real research in a University of Illinois lab on topics such as neuroscience, AI, physics and bioengineering, with seminars, a poster and a final symposium.
pay_detail: No cost except transportation. Housing, meals and a monetary award are provided (the page calls it a fellowship payment; the amount is not stated).
duration: 6 weeks (research began June 17 and ended July 31 in 2026); 30 to 35 hours a week
deadline_text: Applications Closed for Summer 2026.

name: Counselor-in-Training (CIT) Program
what_you_do: Help lead summer day camp activities and assist counselors and campers, set personal goals and meet weekly with other CITs.
pay_detail: No wage is listed on the page; it is described as training for future summer and part-time jobs. Confirm with the contact.
duration: 15 to 20 hours a week, three days a week, June 3 to July 31 in 2026 (8:15 am to 3 pm)
deadline_text: 2026 applications were due March 31, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

name: FRESH Crew Teen Volunteer Days
what_you_do: Join Saturday stewardship days in local parks: collect prairie seed, pull invasive plants and clear trash. No experience needed.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You can earn service hours and references.
duration: 2 hours per event (2 to 4 pm Saturdays)
deadline_text: No registration. Fall 2026 dates: Oct 3, Oct 17, Nov 7, Nov 21, Dec 5 (2 to 4 pm).

name: Youth Event Support Volunteer
what_you_do: Teen volunteers help library staff set up and break down, and help run programs and events for kids and teens.
duration: Ongoing; most needed in summer and on afternoons and weekends in the school year
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: Community Attention Youth Internship Program (CAYIP)
what_you_do: Paid part-time internships at local worksites, with a mandatory CAYIP Academy on workplace skills and a counselor who visits your site at least once a week.
pay_detail: Performance-based stipend up to $15 per hour
duration: School-year sessions: up to 10 hours a week for 8 weeks (Fall 2026: Sept 14 to Nov 8). Summer session: 20 hours a week for 6 weeks.
deadline_text: The page lists four school-year sessions and one summer session for 2026-27 but gives dates only for Fall 2026 (applications Aug 20-28, 2026, now closed). For reference, the Summer 2025 application window was April 1 to May 1, 2025 (5 pm).

name: Lifeguard Training (Charlottesville Parks and Recreation)
org: City of Charlottesville Parks and Recreation, Aquatics
what_you_do: A lifeguard certification class run by the city's aquatics staff. You must pass an in-water pretest, finish online assignments and attend in-class sessions.
pay_detail: Course fee not stated on the page (an optional CPR mask is $15).
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: Session dates were not listed on the page; use the Registration & Tickets link.

name: Recreation Leader in Training (RIT), ages 13 to 15
what_you_do: A mentoring and job-readiness program where 13 to 15 year olds help with park programs such as sports, games, nature and arts and crafts, building leadership, communication and customer service skills.
pay_detail: The program page does not mention pay or a stipend. Confirm with the Park District before you plan around pay.
duration: Spring, fall and winter: 8 weeks, 6 hours a week. Summer: 6 weeks, 30 program days.
deadline_text: 2026 sessions: Winter Jan 12 to Mar 14 (programs viewable online Dec 1, 2025), Spring Apr 6 to Jun 6, Summer Jun 22 to Jul 31, Fall Oct 5 to Dec 11 (viewable online July 27). 2027 dates not posted.

name: Chicago Park District summer jobs (lifeguard, recreation leader, junior laborer)
what_you_do: Teens 16 and up work in the parks as lifeguards, day camp recreation leaders, special recreation leaders (camps for kids and adults with intellectual disabilities) or junior laborers doing landscape work.
pay_detail: 2026 rates: lifeguard $20.50 per hour; recreation leader, special recreation leader and junior laborer $17.77 per hour.
duration: Recreation leaders about 6 weeks, mid-June to early Aug. Junior laborers start April, May or June.
deadline_text: All four 2026 summer positions are marked closed. 2027 dates not posted. The Park District holds free Teen Opportunity Fairs in Feb and March (Feb 21 to Mar 14 in 2026) where teens can apply.

name: Chicago Youth Works (formerly One Summer Chicago): summer jobs
org: City of Chicago Dept. of Family and Support Services
what_you_do: The City's summer youth employment program places young people in paid jobs with partners such as the Park District, CPS, City Colleges, Chicago Housing Authority, the Forest Preserves and Lincoln Park Zoo.
pay_detail: Paid. The pay rate is set by each partner and is not stated on the program pages. Most summer jobs run 20 to 25 hours a week.
duration: At least 6 weeks; in 2026 most programs ran June 22 to July 31
deadline_text: 2026 application ran March 10 to May 29, 2026. 2027 dates not posted; expect late winter or spring.

name: Chicagobility (paid summer career exploration for ages 14 and 15)
org: City of Chicago Dept. of Family and Support Services
what_you_do: A six-week summer program with workforce preparation, financial literacy training and career exploration, built around 120 hours of activities. Participants make a resume and sign up for direct deposit.
pay_detail: Paid stipend for the 120 hours. Amount not stated.
duration: 6 weeks, 120 hours
deadline_text: The 2026 Chicago Youth Works application (which covers 14 to 24 year olds) ran March 10 to May 29, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

name: VolunTEEN Program (Children's Healthcare of Atlanta)
what_you_do: Volunteer in a children's hospital over the summer, at least one 3-hour shift a week for eight weeks. Placements are at Arthur M. Blank, Hughes Spalding or Scottish Rite hospitals.
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost stated on the page.
duration: 8 weeks in June and July (June 8 to July 31 in 2026), one 3-hour day per week, no more than two missed days
deadline_text: The page says the next chance to apply is February 2027; exact open and close dates are not posted yet.

name: CHP Explorer Post (East Sacramento)
what_you_do: You can join an Explorer post for teens who want a law enforcement career. You get training and mentoring from CHP officers.
deadline_text: Rolling.

name: Junior Ambassador Program (high school volunteers)
what_you_do: Serve patients and visitors, support hospital staff and explore health care careers, working one 4 hour shift each week.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: Summer: first week of June to first week of August, 40 hours minimum. Fall and spring: 60 hours minimum. One 4 hour shift a week.
deadline_text: Three cycles a year: summer apply by April 30, fall by August 30, spring by December 30. The page lists month and day only, no year.

name: High School Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Complete tasks under hospital staff supervision in the pediatric setting for a weekly 2 to 3 hour shift, building teamwork and leadership skills.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: Weekly 2 to 3 hour shift; Summer 2026 session
deadline_text: The deadline for the Summer 2026 session has passed. The page says the summer application is usually posted in January, with about two months to finish the packet.

name: Aquatics Jobs: Lifeguard and Pool Staff
what_you_do: Work part-time or seasonal jobs at Cincinnati public pools. Lifeguards keep pool users safe; gate and pool monitors handle customer service and watch behavior around the pool.
pay_detail: Paid; rate not stated on the page
duration: Seasonal and part-time; dates not stated
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the page. A 2026 lifeguard screening registration form is linked.

name: Youth to Work (Y2WK) Summer Jobs
what_you_do: Work a summer job with City departments (such as recreation centers, pools, parks, fire and police cadets) or nonprofit partners, with workshops on workplace etiquette and basic work skills.
pay_detail: Paid; hourly rate not stated on the pages read
duration: Summer; roughly June to early August, dates vary by partner
deadline_text: The program page says the application is usually available February to March. In 2026 the deadline passed in March (WVXU reported about two weeks left on March 10, 2026). 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Library Volunteer Opportunities (ages 12+)
what_you_do: Volunteer at the Main Library or a branch: help with kids and teen events, holds, clerical work, technology help or tutoring.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: 3 months or longer, 2 to 6 hours a week
deadline_text: The library volunteer system says it is accepting new volunteer applications. No deadline is posted.

name: Youth Programs Volunteers
what_you_do: Greet visitors, help guests find their way and cover the museums' gallery spaces, working with museum teams. Teens set their own shifts and can stay until they graduate.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer; perks include free museum admission and parking
duration: Year-round through high school; first summer needs at least six shadowing sessions
deadline_text: Youth volunteers are recruited each year from January through March. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Green Team Youth Summer Jobs
org: Groundwork Ohio River Valley with Cincinnati Parks
what_you_do: Improve and maintain trails, parks and community spaces, remove invasive plants and learn job readiness and natural resource skills for the green industry.
pay_detail: Paid summer job; rate not stated
duration: Summer; length not stated
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the pages read. The City post is undated.

name: ZooTeen Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Volunteer at the Zoo for the summer, including one week of ZooTeen camp and Visitor Engagement shifts, plus Lunch and Learns and events.
pay_detail: $60 non-refundable program fee on acceptance (volunteering is unpaid)
duration: Starts May 31, 2027; 100 hours for first and second year ZooTeens, including a 40 hour camp week
deadline_text: Summer 2027 application is open online Dec 1, 2026 to Jan 31, 2027. Information sessions Nov 16, Dec 14 and Jan 11 (6 to 7 p.m.). Group interviews Feb 27, Feb 28, Mar 13 or Mar 14. Decisions by email April 2, 2027.

name: FARMS Leadership Program
what_you_do: You are in a school-year group that visits farms, conservation sites, agriculture businesses and colleges (at least six field days). You build resume, interview and speaking skills.
pay_detail: No cost or stipend listed on the page.
duration: school year, 6+ field days
deadline_text: No dates posted. Schools sign up as groups.

name: Urban Ag Internships
what_you_do: You get a year-long paid internship at a school garden. It includes weekly garden hours, a workforce class, field trips to farms and guest speakers.
pay_detail: Pay rate not posted on the page.
duration: year-long
deadline_text: No dates posted on the page.

name: CTAE Work-Based Learning, Cobb County School District
what_you_do: Juniors and seniors leave school for one or more class periods to work in a career-related job, internship or youth apprenticeship, earning school credit. They keep a career portfolio and employers send evaluations.
pay_detail: Placements may be paid or non-paid, according to the district page.
duration: A school year; students can be in WBL both junior and senior year. A 90-minute block needs at least 7.5 work hours a week.
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the district page. Ask your school's coordinator for the application window.

name: B.O.S.S. Young Professionals Program (CobbWorks)
org: CobbWorks (Cobb County workforce board, WorkSource Cobb)
what_you_do: A career pathway program with free education tuition, paid work experience, job readiness workshops, career coaching, and GED or diploma help for young adults in Cobb County.
pay_detail: Participants can earn up to $8,500 across the program's activities, according to the program page.
duration: Not stated. Participants enter at any stage.
deadline_text: Year-round. No application dates are posted.

name: College of San Mateo Dual Enrollment and Concurrent Enrollment
what_you_do: Take free college classes at College of San Mateo while in high school. Dual enrollment (through partner high schools) includes free books and materials; concurrent enrollment is free for up to 11 units a semester.
pay_detail: Free. Dual enrollment includes textbooks and materials; concurrent enrollment is free for up to 11 units per semester.
deadline_text: No application deadline stated on the pages read.

name: Summer Reading Challenge VolunTeen
what_you_do: Help library customers sign up for the Summer Reading Challenge, log reading points, hand out prizes and help with programs at a branch.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: June 1 to July 31 (2026 dates)
deadline_text: 2026: application opened April 13 at 3 p.m. and the program ran June 1 to July 31. 2027 dates are not posted. The library's regular volunteer application for Fall 2026 opened August 10.

name: Metro Parks Volunteer Program (Junior Volunteers at Inniswood)
what_you_do: Volunteer in central Ohio parks, for example as a naturalist, trail volunteer or on wildlife projects. Junior Volunteers at Inniswood Metro Gardens help with flowerbeds and children's programs.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: Flexible schedule by assignment and park
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. Volunteer Information sessions are held twice a year; the Inniswood training is held in March.

name: APPS Job Readiness Program
what_you_do: Do paid work with City departments and local businesses, such as helping at summer camps, maintaining parks or supporting golf course operations, with mentorship, skill building and career planning.
pay_detail: $15 an hour, up to 20 hours a week
duration: Mostly summer; some participants may continue in fall and winter
deadline_text: 2026 participant applications ran Feb 2 to Feb 17, 2026 and are closed. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: City Leaders Academy
what_you_do: Learn leadership, teamwork, problem solving and service through monthly meet-ups from fall to spring, with a mandatory family orientation and an end-of-year ceremony.
pay_detail: No pay; cost not stated on the page
duration: Sept orientation, then 12 monthly meet-ups Oct 2026 to May 2027; ceremony May 15, 2027
deadline_text: 2026-27 applications were due 5 p.m. Wednesday, July 1, 2026. 2027-28 dates are not posted.

name: Seasonal Lifeguard
what_you_do: Currently hiring lifeguards for seasonal positions.
pay_detail: $20 an hour (seasonal)
duration: Summer season; dates not stated
deadline_text: The page says the City is hiring seasonal lifeguards for the summer. No application dates are posted.

name: Work Readiness Training University (WRTU)
what_you_do: Take part in a paid summer youth internship program that builds empowerment, innovation, high performance and civic engagement skills with employer partners.
pay_detail: Paid for summer involvement; rate not stated
duration: Summer; length not stated
deadline_text: No application dates are posted on the program page.

name: ZooAide Teen Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Help guests and learn about conservation careers, with an emphasis on zoo and aquarium customer service. Direct animal contact is minimal.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
deadline_text: The 2026 season application has ended. The page says 2027 ZooAide applications will be posted in early 2027.

name: Computer History Museum Teen Volunteer Intern Program
what_you_do: Teens in grades 9 to 12 go behind the scenes with the education team, research tech history, meet Silicon Valley professionals and lead tours and activities.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page
duration: Not stated on the page
deadline_text: Applications are currently closed. Join the interest list to hear about the next round.

name: Congressional App Challenge
what_you_do: Build an app in any language and submit it to your House district. Winners are shown at the US Capitol.
pay_detail: Free
duration: Build time before the deadline
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline for registering and submitting is October 26, 2026.

name: Contra Costa College Dual Enrollment
what_you_do: You can take free college classes (no tuition, books or enrollment fees) if you attend West Contra Costa USD, Leadership Public Schools, Griffin Technology Academies or Middle College High School on campus.
pay_detail: Free: no tuition, textbook or enrollment fees.
duration: Per term
deadline_text: Rolling by term.

name: Contra Costa County Library Teen Volunteers

pay_detail: Expected $4,800 for 2026 (tuition, materials, housing and Monday to Friday meals). Partial and need-based scholarships available.
duration: Four weeks (2026: July 6 to 31), residential, home on weekends
deadline_text: 2026: reviewed first come, first served from February 2026; completed application, including solutions to the problems, by March 31 if seeking a scholarship; financial aid applications by April 15, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Teen / High School Volunteers, Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital
org: RWJBarnabas Health, Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital
what_you_do: Greet, direct and escort visitors, visit patients on nursing floors, and help with patient discharges at the hospital's New Brunswick or Somerset campus.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The required urine drug screen is free to the volunteer; no other costs are listed.
duration: Minimum 100 hours of service per year; the hospital hopes for 2 to 3 hours a week. Shifts mornings, afternoons and evenings, 7 days a week.
deadline_text: No application deadline or dates are listed on the page.

grades: High school students who completed a high school biology course
name: Waksman Institute Summer Experience (WISE)
org: Waksman Institute of Microbiology, Rutgers University
what_you_do: Two weeks of lab work and bioinformatics on duckweed DNA at the Waksman Institute; students' vetted sequences are published on GenBank with their names.
pay_detail: $2,200 for the in-person WISE (non-refundable, due 2 weeks after approval). A virtual vWISE costs $600.
duration: Two weeks, Monday to Friday (2026 sessions: June 22 to July 2, July 27 to August 7; vWISE August 10 to 21)
deadline_text: 2026 application opened February 2, 2026 and was first come, first served (sessions expected to fill). Application forms for the Summer 2027 WISE Programs will be posted in late January 2027.

name: Governor's School of New Jersey in Engineering and Technology
org: Rutgers School of Engineering / State of New Jersey
what_you_do: A free, four-week residential summer program for rising seniors: four courses, a small team research and design project, company visits and a final research symposium.
pay_detail: Free to students and families (tuition, room and board paid by donations). FAQ says students bring a $65 key deposit returned at the end. The FAQ page is undated.
duration: About 4 weeks, starting close to the beginning of July, with about 40 hours of prep work beforehand
deadline_text: 2027 application not posted on the pages read. The state page (updated 11/13/25) said 2026 applications were open; decisions are emailed in early April. Ask your school counselor about the school nomination deadline.

name: Newport Beach Public Library Teen Volunteers
what_you_do: Help in the Children's Department (Summer Reading Program, craft materials), write book reviews from home, or join the Young Adult Advisory Council.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 20 hours of service per year. Children's Department shifts are 1 to 2 hours a week. YAAC also meets monthly.
deadline_text: No deadline. Applications are first-come, first-served and accepted as needed.

name: Newport Beach Teen Leader Program
org: City of Newport Beach Recreation and Senior Services
what_you_do: Volunteer next to city Recreation staff at summer day camps, Pint-Sized Camp, the Marina Park Sailing & Boating Center and city events, building leadership and work skills.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Selected teens pay a $206 program fee for 2026.
duration: The 2026 session; exact length not stated
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed Thursday, May 1, 2026. Next year's dates are not posted.

name: Marine Teens Internship
org: Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County (NHMLAC)
what_you_do: Build a marine science project and share it with museum visitors. You learn about museum research, collections and careers, and practice public speaking.
pay_detail: Interns are paid museum employees. The hourly rate is not stated.
duration: Spring: select Saturdays in April and May (about 10 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.). Summer: six weeks in June and July, 24 hours a week.
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back in February 2027 for the application link and deadline.

name: Waterpark seasonal jobs with free training
org: NOVA Parks (Northern Virginia Regional Park Authority)
city: Northern Virginia (Fairfax, Alexandria and Arlington waterparks)
what_you_do: Work summer jobs at a NOVA Parks waterpark as an attendant, lifeguard, water safety instructor or cook. Uniforms and training are free.
pay_detail: Pay rates not stated on the page. Free uniforms and free training.
duration: Seasonal (summer)
deadline_text: Page says NOVA Parks is hiring; no deadline stated.

name: NOVAworks Young Adult Services
city: Sunnyvale, CA (serves San Mateo County and northern Santa Clara County)
what_you_do: You can get free career coaching and training if you are an eligible young adult. You can also take a paid internship of about 400 hours if you are 18 or older. If you are 17, you can start with coaching and work readiness.
pay_detail: Coaching is free. Paid internships start at $19.50 per hour (Sunnyvale minimum wage), at least $7,800 for 400 hours. Internships are for ages 18 and up.
duration: 4 to 5 weeks of career readiness first, then an internship (most interns work 10 to 20 hours a week)
deadline_text: Open enrollment. No deadline posted.

name: National Park Service Youth Conservation Corps (YCC)
city: Participating national parks (see the NPS park list)
what_you_do: You can get a paid summer conservation job at a national park, working outdoors on park projects. Each park runs its own program.
pay_detail: At least the higher of the state or federal minimum wage, usually for a 40 hour week
duration: 8 to 10 weeks (can go up to 18), usually 40 hours per week
deadline_text: Applications for the 2027 season open in late January or early February 2027. Closing dates are set by each park and are not posted.

name: Garden Apprentice Program (GAP)
what_you_do: Grow and harvest food in the Children's Garden, learn botany, and teach garden lessons to kids ages 4 to 12. You move up through four tiers over the years.
pay_detail: Tier 1 $600, Tier 2 $700, Tier 3 $800 as a one-time nontaxable reimbursement in November, plus a $75 perfect attendance bonus. Tier 4 (by invitation after Tier 3) is a part-time staff job at $17 per hour. No fee to join.
duration: 9 months, March to November 2027 (about 4 to 6 hours a week in spring and fall, 20 to 25 hours a week in summer; about 190 to 220 hours total).
deadline_text: Submit your materials before Dec 4, 2026 to be invited to an interview. No final deadline is posted. Info session Sat Oct 17, 2026, 11 a.m. to 1 p.m.

name: Pre-College Programs: NYC Commuter Summer
org: Columbia University School of Professional Studies
what_you_do: Take a college-level course on Columbia's campus (70+ courses in a dozen subject areas, about 4 hours of class each weekday) and go home at night. You earn a certificate of participation and an evaluation letter.
grades: Entering grades 9 to 12, or freshman year of college
pay_detail: 1-week session $2,883. 3-week session $6,381. Plus an $95 application fee and $50 or more for course materials. Deposit $1,000 (1-week) or $2,000 (3-week) is credited toward the cost. These are estimates pending trustee approval.
duration: 1 week (Jun 21 to 25, 2027) or 3 weeks (Jun 28 to Jul 16, 2027; more sessions listed on the dates page).
deadline_text: Summer 2027 applications open mid-November 2026. Early registration deadline Feb 1, 2027. General application deadline Apr 1, 2027 for the NYC Commuter sessions.

name: Summer Innovation Intensives
what_you_do: Three weeks on the Cornell Tech campus learning AI, ethical coding, data science and product innovation, then pitching a project at a final showcase. No coding experience needed. You earn two Cornell credits.
grades: Finished sophomore year of high school or later
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page (students earn 2 Cornell credits). Ask summer@tech.cornell.edu before applying.
duration: 3 weeks, commuter only (no housing). Exact 2027 dates are not stated on the program page.
deadline_text: The summer 2027 application will open in winter 2026. The summer 2026 application is closed. No deadline posted. Rolling review.

name: Ladders for Leaders
org: NYC Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD)
what_you_do: Paid professional summer internships with companies, nonprofits and city agencies in NYC, after about 30 hours of pre-employment training. It is part of SYEP.
grades: Rising high school seniors and college students
pay_detail: At least $16.50 per hour in 2025 (2025 FAQ). 2026 pay is not stated on the page.
duration: 6 weeks, 25 to 40 hours a week (2025 FAQ)
deadline_text: DYCD page says the deadline for the last cycle was extended to January 16, 2026. Next cycle dates are not posted.

name: Learn & Earn
org: NYC Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD)
what_you_do: Career exploration and academic support for high school juniors and seniors: college application help, work readiness training, service learning and leadership activities, plus a paid six-week summer internship.
pay_detail: Paid six-week summer internship. Rate not stated on the page.
duration: Year-round program with a six-week paid summer internship
deadline_text: Page says enrollment dates are September 1 to 30 (year not stated). That window has passed for this fall.

name: Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
org: NYC Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD)
what_you_do: Ages 14-15 do paid, project-based career activities. Ages 16 and up work paid summer jobs placed by SYEP providers across the city, and learn work-readiness and financial literacy skills.
pay_detail: Ages 16-24 (2026): $17.00 per hour, 25 hours a week. Ages 14-15 (2026): up to $700 for about 12.5 hours a week.
duration: 6 weeks
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed March 13, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted yet.

name: Work, Learn & Grow (WLG)
org: NYC Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD)
what_you_do: A school-year follow-up to SYEP. You take a CUNY course, join skill-building sessions and do a paid internship, with the chance to earn college credit.
pay_detail: New York State minimum wage, paid every two weeks (DYCD FAQ).
duration: 22 weeks, Oct 26, 2026 to Apr 3, 2027, 250 hours total
deadline_text: The WLG application page lists a deadline of October 9, 2026. The FAQ PDF lists the application period as Sept 8 to Oct 2, 2026, so confirm with your SYEP provider.

name: Summer Volunteer Program for High School Students
what_you_do: Summer volunteering in non-clinical roles across Montefiore hospital campuses and health centers in the Bronx. Placement depends on hospital needs and your availability.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering.
duration: Summer session runs June to September; minimum 100 hours; each session at least 3 to 4 hours.
deadline_text: The page still shows Summer 2025 postings with high school applications January 1 to May 31. No 2027 dates are posted. Onboarding takes about a month, so apply early in spring.

name: Junior Medical Program (JuMP) and high school volunteering
what_you_do: JuMP is a 6-week summer program where 15 to 17 year olds learn from healthcare staff in clinical and non-clinical areas. High schoolers can also join as Unit Support volunteers who visit patients and help orient them.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page lists no JuMP cost or pay.
duration: JuMP: 6 weeks, 100 hours. Unit Support: one 3-hour shift a week; the page lists a 100 hour minimum for high school students.
deadline_text: JuMP applications are accepted January 1 to March 1 (no year given on the page; expect Jan 1 to Mar 1, 2027). Space is limited. The process can take 4 to 8 weeks.

name: NYBG High School Explainer Program
what_you_do: Start as a volunteer intern in the Everett Children's Adventure Garden. You lead hands-on plant and nature activities for kids and families and do a citizen science plant study. Later paid tiers exist.
pay_detail: Intern tier is unpaid volunteering (OMNY card help for transit can be provided). Later tiers (Advanced Explainer, Mentor, Senior) are paid part-time jobs; the page gives no hourly rate.
duration: Spring 2027 internship: one 4.5 hour Saturday or Sunday shift each week, Mar 20 to Jun 19, 2027 (minimum 105 service hours), plus 4 required training days (Mar 6, 7, 13, 14, 2027).
deadline_text: Spring 2027 application closes Saturday Nov 14, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Open House Sat Nov 7, 2026, 1 to 2 p.m. (RSVP by Oct 30). A fall session also runs; its applications open late spring.

name: Summer Only Volunteering
what_you_do: Volunteer in a hospital for the summer in a role matched to the campus and the department. Placements vary by campus, so you list your preferred program and location on the application.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering.
duration: Minimum 120 service hours over the summer.
deadline_text: Applications are accepted January 1 to March 31 (the page gives no year; expect Jan 1 to Mar 31, 2027).

name: Summer Volunteer Program, Manhattan Campus
what_you_do: Volunteer in hospital lobbies, outpatient clinics, children's units or other areas at Tisch, Kimmel, Hassenfeld Children's or Perlmutter. Roles are customer-service support, not clinical work or shadowing.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The FAQ says no pay or school credit is given.
duration: 8 weeks, two 6-hour shifts a week (100 service hours total).
deadline_text: Applications open annually January 15 to February 15 (or until capacity is reached). The page gives no year; expect Jan 15 to Feb 15, 2027.

name: ARISE (Applied Research Innovations in Science and Engineering)
what_you_do: Spend a summer as a research assistant in one of many NYU STEM labs, working with faculty and grad students. You build presentation skills and present at a final colloquium.
grades: Rising juniors and seniors (10th or 11th graders applying)
pay_detail: Free. A $2,000 stipend is paid for completing the program.
duration: 10 weeks: about 4 weeks of remote after-school workshops in June, then 6 weeks of in-person lab work (about 150 hours of lab experience). Summer 2026 ran Jun 1 to Aug 14, 2026.
deadline_text: Summer 2026 deadline was Feb 27, 2026 at 5 p.m. Summer 2027 dates are not posted yet.

name: Summer Science Research Program (SSRP)
what_you_do: Seven weeks of team-based, mentored lab research on campus with scientists from Rockefeller, MSK and Weill Cornell. You choose a question, collect data and present a poster at the end.
grades: Current high school juniors and seniors
pay_detail: Free to apply and attend. An OMNY card covers NYC transit. Stipends are not guaranteed; need-based stipends may go to students with financial hardship who meet all attendance rules.
duration: 7 weeks, Mon Jun 21 to Thu Aug 5, 2027, full time (about 35 hours a week, roughly 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
deadline_text: Applications for SSRP 2027 open Oct 15, 2026. The deadline is not posted yet. The last cycle closed Fri Jan 2, 2026 (letters of recommendation due Jan 5), with Zoom interviews in March and decisions in April.

name: Discovery Guide Youth Volunteer Program
org: Wildlife Conservation Society (Bronx Zoo, Central Park, Prospect Park and Queens Zoos, New York Aquarium)
what_you_do: Teach zoo and aquarium visitors about animals through fun activities, help with education programs and support WCS conservation campaigns. You can move up through the program over the seasons.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. WCS says youth volunteers earn over 100 hours of community service.
duration: Usually a spring session and a summer session; hours not stated.
deadline_text: Not accepting applications now. Applications for the next cycle open in late December 2026 for Spring 2027. No closing date posted.

name: Youth Insights (YI Artists, Arts Careers, Introductions, Leaders)
what_you_do: Free art and arts-career programs for NYC high schoolers. Graduates can apply to YI Leaders, a yearlong paid after-school internship where teens plan public programs, lead gallery tours and write for the teen blog.
grades: Grades 9 to 12 (varies by program; YI Leaders is grades 11 and 12)
pay_detail: YI Leaders is a paid internship; the page does not state the amount.
duration: YI Artists: one semester after school. Summer programs: length not stated. YI Leaders: yearlong, 3 to 10 hours a week.
deadline_text: YI Artists (this semester) deadline was Sep 9, 2026 (extended). YI Arts Careers and YI Introductions list no 2026 deadline and reopen in Summer 2027. No YI Leaders deadline is posted.

name: Career and Technical Education (CTE) high schools
what_you_do: Career-focused classes in 14 areas such as healthcare, digital technology, construction and hospitality. Includes work-based learning like job shadowing, internships and apprenticeships, plus industry certifications.
pay_detail: Part of the school day at no cost. Some work-based learning (such as apprenticeships) can be paid, but pay is not stated on this page.
duration: Grades 9 to 12
deadline_text: Enroll through the regular NYC high school admissions process. Dates are not stated on the CTE page.

name: Career Readiness and Modern Youth Apprenticeship (CRMYA)
org: NYC Public Schools with CareerWise New York
what_you_do: Career readiness classes in 9th and 10th grade, then juniors apply for a paid apprenticeship at a workplace for 2 to 3 years while finishing high school, with a state-registered credential.
pay_detail: Paid work experience. Pay rate is not stated on the page.
duration: 2 to 3 year apprenticeship starting junior year
deadline_text: Dates are not stated. Juniors apply during the school year; ask your school.

name: Mayor's Summer Youth Employment Program (MSYEP)
org: City of Oakland, Oakland Workforce Development Board, and partner nonprofits
what_you_do: You get paid summer work experience of up to about 100 hours, with job readiness training, through partner nonprofits. You apply to the partner group, not the City.
pay_detail: At least Oakland's minimum wage; exact rate set by each partner
duration: Up to 100 paid hours (varies by partner)
deadline_text: Deadlines vary by partner. For Summer 2026 one partner (ACOE) closed recruitment June 18, 2026. 2027 dates not posted; check partner sites in early 2027.

name: Oakland Workforce Development Board Youth Summer Jobs (Lao Family, YEP, Trybe)
org: Oakland Workforce Development Board (City of Oakland)
what_you_do: You can get job readiness training, work-based learning and paid work experience through one of three partner agencies, if you are an Oakland youth.
pay_detail: Not stated on this page; the City's MSYEP page says at least Oakland's minimum wage
deadline_text: No dates posted. Contact the partners for the current cycle.

name: Oakland Parks, Recreation and Youth Development (OPRYD) Part-Time Jobs
what_you_do: You can apply for part-time and seasonal City recreation jobs, such as recreation aide, recreation leader, recreation specialist, sports official, lifeguard, water safety instructor and pool staff.
pay_detail: Not posted on the page; see each job posting
duration: Varies by posting; mostly seasonal
deadline_text: Deadline Oct 25, 2026 for Spring/Summer 2027 starts; Feb 7, 2027 for Summer 2027 starts; Aug 8, 2027 for Fall/Winter 2027 starts.

name: Oakland Public Library Teen Advisory Board (TAB)
what_you_do: You can join a monthly teen group that works with library staff on projects and programs and earns service credit. It meets at Main (TeenZone), 81st Ave, Asian, Cesar Chavez, Dimond and Rockridge branches.
duration: One meeting a month
deadline_text: Rolling

name: Oakland Public Library Teen Volunteer Program
what_you_do: You help at a library branch with teen programs, social media, book and film picks, and art and design projects. The hours count as community service.
duration: Shifts when the library is open; the form asks for morning and afternoon or evening availability, any day of the week
deadline_text: Rolling. Not every branch has space at all times.

name: Teen Summer Internship (California Trail Interpretation)
what_you_do: You spend about 200 hours over 7 weeks teaching guests in the Habitarium and California Trail. Up to 6 interns are chosen.
pay_detail: $50 non-refundable fee when selected (aid available). No stipend is listed.
duration: About 200 hours over 7 weeks (June 10 to July 28 or Aug 1 in 2026); shifts 9 am to 4:30 pm, Sunday to Wednesday or Wednesday to Saturday
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Teen Wild Guides
what_you_do: Teens learn to teach visitors about animals at the Valley Children's Zoo, run the petting yard, and can later help keepers on service projects.
pay_detail: $50 first year, then $25 a year; financial aid on request
duration: School year: every other weekend. Summer: about once a week. Shifts 9:30 am to 4 pm.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 info meetings Aug 15 and 16, applications due Sept 1, 2026, trainings Sept 26 and Oct 4. The page says applications are accepted year-round and later ones are reviewed in the next enrollment period.

name: ZooCamp Teen Assistant and Teen Interns
what_you_do: Help run summer day camp at the zoo. Teen Assistants volunteer. Teacher and Administrative Interns (grades 11 and 12, with camp experience) earn a $400 weekly stipend.
pay_detail: Teen Assistant unpaid (community service hours). Interns: $400 per week stipend, assuming full attendance.
duration: 1-week sessions, Mon to Fri, June 1 to Aug 7 (2026); at least 3 sessions (Administrative Intern: 3 sessions in a row)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Feb 1 and closed April 1, 2026 at 5pm. Summer 2027 dates not posted yet; the page says to check back.

name: OC Fair & Event Center Jobs (annual OC Fair)
what_you_do: Work at the annual OC Fair or at events held year-round at the fairgrounds, in indoor or outdoor jobs.
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page
duration: The OC Fair runs for a few weeks in summer. Fairgrounds also hosts 150+ events a year.
deadline_text: No hiring dates posted on the jobs page for 2027.

name: OC Public Libraries Teen Volunteer
city: Orange County, CA (any OC Public Libraries branch)
what_you_do: Help a local library branch organize library materials and take part in library events. Shifts are flexible and include weekdays and weekends.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Flexible shifts, set by the branch
deadline_text: No deadline. Openings are limited and depend on each branch.

name: OC Workforce Development Board READY S.E.T. OC (WIOA Young Adult Program)
what_you_do: Get help with tutoring, career exploration, paid or unpaid work experience, job skills training, mentoring and college planning through county service providers.
pay_detail: Work experience can be paid or unpaid. Wage not stated on the page.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Start by filling out the interest form.

name: OUSD Linked Learning Internships
org: Oakland Unified School District, High School Linked Learning Office
what_you_do: You can find paid summer internships and after-school internships for Oakland Unified high school students. The district lists them by employer, with dates and pay. Your pathway teachers can also connect you to internships.
pay_detail: Summer internships are paid; amounts vary by employer (see the district list). The district's 2024 listing said Peralta Summer Institute students got a stipend; the current Peralta page only says classes are free.
duration: Varies by employer
deadline_text: The district updates its summer internship list weekly from January to May. The page still shows Summer 2024 forms; 2027 dates not posted.

name: OUSD Linked Learning: Pathways, Internships and Work Permits
org: Oakland Unified School District, High School Linked Learning Office
what_you_do: You can get help with career pathways, internships and job placement, plus dual enrollment (college classes while in high school) with Peralta Colleges. The office also processes work permits for Oakland Unified students.
pay_detail: Rate not posted (checked 2026-10-07)
deadline_text: Ongoing; talk to your school's pathway or career counselor. No dates posted.

name: Palo Alto Art Center Summer Camp Counselor in Training
org: City of Palo Alto Art Center
what_you_do: Help art teachers run kids' and teen summer art camps for at least one week, in a morning or afternoon session. You manage the classroom, encourage campers and prep art supplies.
duration: At least 1 week
deadline_text: CIT and Lead CIT registration opens Feb 4, 2027 with Enjoy! summer camp registration. No closing date stated.

name: Teen Library Advisory Board (Palo Alto City Library)
what_you_do: Teens in grades 8 to 12 volunteer with the library through the advisory board. Each semester you pick an activity such as planning a teen program, helping at an outreach event or writing a booklist.
duration: Fall (Sept to Dec), Winter/Spring (Jan to May) and Summer (June to Aug) terms
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back in December 2026 to apply for Winter/Spring 2027.

name: Teen Advisory Board (Mitchell Park Teen Services)
org: City of Palo Alto, Mitchell Park Teen Services
what_you_do: You can join a group of 15 to 20 high school students who plan and lead events for teens in Palo Alto.
deadline_text: The page mentions a deadline but gives no date or year. The only dates found were in a 2023 city article.

name: Palo Alto Youth Council (PAYC)
org: City of Palo Alto, Mitchell Park Teen Services
what_you_do: High school students (15 to 20 on the council) act as youth ambassadors to the Palo Alto City Council on teen concerns like mental health, civic engagement and community events.
deadline_text: The page says the application opens July 2027. No closing date stated.

name: Pathful Explore (virtual career exploration)
what_you_do: You can explore careers online through videos, assessments and virtual chats with professionals. Your school has to license Pathful for you to use it.
pay_detail: Free to students if your school licenses it; pricing is not on the site
duration: Self-paced
deadline_text: Depends on your school.

name: Peralta Colleges Dual Enrollment (Laney, Merritt, Berkeley City, College of Alameda)
what_you_do: Take free college classes while in high school, on a Peralta campus or through classes arranged with your school. Courses go on your permanent college transcript.
pay_detail: Tuition and fees excused. Unit caps: CCAP 15 units fall or spring; other dual enrollment 11 units fall or spring; 9 units in summer.
duration: Per term (fall, spring, summer)
deadline_text: No deadlines posted. Register each term.

name: Summer Youth Enrichment Program (SYEP)
org: Prince George's County Government, Office of Human Resources Management
what_you_do: Get a paid 6-week summer job with Prince George's County Government or a county partner, with job readiness training and career exploration.
pay_detail: Hourly and stipend opportunities are available (rate not stated in the county release I could read).
duration: 6 weeks (Jul 6 to Aug 14 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications Mar 1 to Mar 31, 2026; program Jul 6 to Aug 14, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Youth volunteers at Summer Playtime and Summer Day Camps
org: M-NCPPC Department of Parks and Recreation, Prince George's County
what_you_do: Volunteer at a Summer Playtime program (age 14) or a Summer Day Camp (age 15) for 12 to 15 hours a week and earn student service learning hours.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Approved for Prince George's County Public Schools Student Service Learning hours.
duration: 12 to 15 hours per week
deadline_text: Volunteer applications are accepted online from March 1-May 1. The page gives no year.

name: M-NCPPC Youth Advisory Council (YAC)
org: M-NCPPC Department of Parks and Recreation, Prince George's County
what_you_do: Join about 20 high school youth who advise the parks department, plan teen events and community service projects, and join leadership conferences and field trips.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn student service learning credits or community service hours.
duration: School year; meetings in person at community centers and online
deadline_text: No application deadline stated.

name: Library volunteering and VolunTEEN
org: Prince George's County Memorial Library System
what_you_do: Help at a branch as a library, computer, facility or program aide, or earn up to 6 service hours through VolunTEEN. Teens over the age of 15 can help in the Kids Achieve Club homework program.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Student service learning hours are available.
duration: Temporary (limited) or regular (at least 6 months) schedules
deadline_text: No deadline. Kids Achieve Club interviews: June for September programs, November for January programs.

name: Volunteer Program, Academy of Natural Sciences
org: Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University
what_you_do: Help in collections departments, the Patrick Center lab, the Bird Safe Philly bird-collision program, or Nature at Noon walks; roles vary and not all are listed as open to teens.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Regular time from half a day to several days a week, for at least one year
deadline_text: No deadline listed.

name: Bloomberg Arts Internship (BAI)
what_you_do: Paid summer internship at an arts and culture organization in Philadelphia, with professional development, mentoring and college and career readiness sessions.
pay_detail: $20+ per hour for Summer 2026, plus transportation and meal support
duration: Eight weeks, up to 35 hours a week (2026: June 19 to August 14); select interns may continue in a school-year program up to 10 hours a week
deadline_text: The page posts no intern application dates. Its only application notice is for worksite hosts: Summer 2026 applications are officially closed.

name: Career Connected Learning PHL (C2L-PHL) Summer Program
org: City of Philadelphia Office of Children and Families, with JEVS Human Services
what_you_do: City-funded paid service learning, project-based learning and internships, with career exploration, mentoring, professional development and job shadowing.
pay_detail: Stipend on a prepaid debit card, paid every other week; total $1,300 to $1,500 depending on the program (hourly rate not listed).
duration: Summer program (plus school-year programming)
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed. FAQ: summer applications open between March and April each year.

grades: Rising high school juniors and seniors with a background in biology, chemistry or research
name: Neuroscience Camp for High School Students, Drexel
org: Drexel University Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences and Professional Studies
what_you_do: A 10-day commuter camp with lectures and lab experiences on current topics in neuroscience.
duration: 10 days, in-person commuter (2026: July 20 to 31)
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was April 3, 2026. The page says 2027 Summer Institutes information will be posted this winter.

grades: Apply as a high school freshman (grade 9)
name: STEM Scholars, The Franklin Institute
what_you_do: A free four-year STEM program for students starting in 9th grade, with STEM programming each year; rising seniors are paid for a 10-week lab research experience.
pay_detail: Free to students; rising seniors are paid for lab research (rate not stated). Fees covered by donors.
duration: Four years, grades 9 to 12; research window of 10 weeks between late June and early September
deadline_text: Applications for the next freshman cohort are currently closed; check back for the 2027 class. FAQ says applications usually open late September or early October and are due mid-December.

name: Become a Lifeguard, Philadelphia Parks and Recreation
