what_you_do: Help professional educators run summer camps for Pre-K through 8th grade at the museum.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page says you gain work experience and/or college credit.
duration: Summer camp season; exact dates not stated
deadline_text: Page says recruitment for camp aides begins in May. No 2027 dates posted.

name: Teen Team Program Assistant
org: San Diego Public Library (City of San Diego)
what_you_do: Join a branch Teen Team. Help library staff plan and lead programs, support teen outreach at community events, and work on special projects.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Apply any time through the City volunteer system.

name: San Diego Workforce Partnership youth career services
what_you_do: Sign up for free career centers that offer training, one-on-one coaching and, for some people, paid on-the-job work experience.
pay_detail: Services are free. Some opportunities include paid training or paid on-the-job work experience; rates are not stated.
duration: Varies by program
deadline_text: No deadline. The online application takes about 10 to 15 minutes, then staff contact you about next steps.

name: San Jose Middle College (San Jose City College)
org: San Jose Unified School District with San Jose City College
what_you_do: Juniors and seniors take 2 to 3 free college classes (6 to 9 college credits) plus 4 high school classes on the San Jose City College campus, and earn a high school diploma plus transferable college credit.
pay_detail: Free college classes (6 to 9 college credits). The page does not state other costs.
duration: Junior and senior years (the page does not state a fixed length)
deadline_text: Not stated on the San Jose City College page. Ask the Middle College office for the application timeline.

name: San Jose Public Library Teen Volunteers (Teens Reach, Teen Book Reviewer)
what_you_do: Join Teens Reach, the library youth council, to help with kids crafts and Summer Learning sign-ups and to speak up as a library advisor. Or earn service hours by writing book reviews as a Teen Book Reviewer.
deadline_text: Rolling. Each branch has its own Teens Reach sign-up. No single deadline.

name: San Jose Works
org: City of San Jose (work2future and Mayor's Gang Prevention Task Force)
what_you_do: You can get paid work experience and job help in San Jose. If you are 14 to 18 and face barriers to work, you can be placed in paid jobs and training. Job services are open to ages 16 to 29.
pay_detail: Rate not posted (checked 2026-10-07)
deadline_text: No deadline posted on the city pages. Apply any time with the online youth application.

name: San Jose Youth Commission and Youth Advisory Council
what_you_do: Teens advise the San Jose Mayor and City Council on youth issues. The Youth Advisory Council (YAC) is open now; Youth Commission recruitment is closed.
duration: Two-year term
deadline_text: Youth Advisory Council (open now): no deadline posted. Youth Commission (closed): recruitment is closed, no reopening date posted.

duration: At least 4 months
name: San Leandro Library Teen Volunteers
what_you_do: You help library staff run programs for younger kids, or help with kit assembly, shelving and displays. You work one shift of 2 to 3 hours a week.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back in November 2026. Summer applications open in mid March, per the summer page.

name: San Leandro Youth Advisory Commission
org: City of San Leandro Recreation and Parks
what_you_do: You give the City Council feedback on issues that affect young people and help run city events like Pumpkin Splash and the Egg Hunt.
deadline_text: The page does not say when applications open.

name: Jobs for Youth (County of San Mateo)
org: County of San Mateo Human Resources
what_you_do: You can take free job-skills workshops and use a members-only job and internship board. Twenty $2,000 scholarships a year are available for San Mateo County youth, and the county summer internship is for ages 18 to 21.
pay_detail: Workshops and job board are free. Twenty $2,000 scholarships each year. Pay for the county summer internship is not stated on the pages I read.
duration: County summer internship: June to August, about 8 to 10 weeks, 20 to 40 hours a week
deadline_text: Membership: register any time. Summer internship: 2026 applications are closed; the page says next summer opens early 2027 (no date posted). Scholarship deadline not stated.

name: San Mateo County Libraries Teen Volunteers
what_you_do: Teens shelve books, help with kids' crafts and STEM programs, join outreach events or support the makerspace.
duration: 6 months or 1 semester
deadline_text: Ongoing. Openings vary by branch and there may be a waiting period.

name: SPARK High School Internship
org: Sanford Burnham Prebys Medical Discovery Institute
what_you_do: Spend six summer weeks as a fully paid intern in a biomedical research lab.
pay_detail: Described as fully paid; the page does not state an amount.
duration: 6 weeks, starting mid-June
deadline_text: Next application dates not posted on the page. Use the Request Info form or email the program director.

name: Santa Ana Zoo Volunteers (including Zoo Buddies)
org: Santa Ana Zoo (City of Santa Ana)
what_you_do: Volunteer at the zoo, either as a short-term Zoo Greeter or in a long-term role. Younger teens can join as a Zoo Buddies pair with a parent or guardian.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Short-term: 40 hours or less (Greeter shifts Fri to Sun, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.). Long-term: more than 40 hours (shifts every day, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
deadline_text: No deadline. Long-term volunteers do an online and an in-person orientation offered every other month.

name: Teaching Assistant Program (Santa Barbara Museum of Art)
what_you_do: Assist a Teaching Artist in art classes and camps for kids: prepare materials, help with hands-on art-making, and act as a role model. Includes an orientation and mentoring.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Counts toward required community service hours.
duration: Per class or camp: Winter After-School Class Tuesdays Jan 12 to Feb 16, 2027 (3:30-5:15 PM); Spring Camp Mar 29 to Apr 2, 2027 (9 AM-3 PM)
deadline_text: Winter After-School Class: apply by Dec 29, 2026 (confirmations Jan 5, 2027). Spring Camp: apply by Mar 15, 2027 (confirmations Mar 22, 2027).

name: Counselors in Training (Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History)
org: Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History
what_you_do: Help run Nature Adventures summer camps for young children at the Museum and Sea Center: crafts, exhibit visits and activities, while earning community service hours and learning to teach.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours. $20 uniform shirt (waived with SNAP/CalFresh EBT).
duration: At least 3 full weeks of camp (2026 camps ran June 15 to Aug 14)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened April 1 and were due April 30, 2026. CIT training was June 12, 2026. Next cycle dates are not posted.

grades: Must be in 8th or 9th grade (or that age) to apply
name: Quasars to Sea Stars (Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History)
org: Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History
what_you_do: A three-to-four year program for high school teens: museum studies classes, learning from scientists, camping and field trips, and volunteering. After 60 community service hours you become a paid Museum employee.
pay_detail: Unpaid for the first 60 community service hours, then paid Museum employee shifts. The pay rate is not stated.
duration: 3 to 4 years; stay active year-round until graduation
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications were due April 3, 2026, with in-person interviews in April and orientation week June 21-27, 2026. The page says applications for 2026 opened Feb 1, 2026. Next cycle dates are not posted.

name: VolunTEENS (Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History)
org: Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History
what_you_do: Staff interpretive tables and science games for guests in the Museum's Backyard, Butterfly Pavilion or Observatory on summer weekends, and earn community service hours.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours for the SBUSD graduation requirement. Uniform shirt purchase required (waived with SNAP/CalFresh EBT).
duration: Up to 16 two-hour weekend shifts, Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day (2026: May 23 to Sept 6)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened April 1 and were due April 30, 2026. Training was May 16-17, 2026. Next cycle dates are not posted.

name: Junior Counselor Program (Parks and Recreation)
org: City of Santa Barbara Parks and Recreation
what_you_do: Help summer camp counselors with daily activities while earning volunteer service hours and building leadership skills.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteer service hours.
duration: Summer camp season; length not stated
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the page. Use the Register link or call Parks and Recreation at 805-564-5418.

name: Parks and Recreation Seasonal Jobs (lifeguard, camp staff)
org: City of Santa Barbara Parks and Recreation
what_you_do: Seasonal and part-time positions that help build valuable workplace skills and experience. Titles listed: Lifeguard, Camp Counselor, Recreation Leader, Seasonal Program Staff.
pay_detail: Hourly, set by position. A March 2024 City notice listed $18.78 to $23.92 an hour for lifeguards, camp counselors and swim instructors; check the current posting.
duration: Summer camps and pools; aquatics hires through the year with more hiring before summer
deadline_text: Aquatics hires year-round; summer hiring is announced in the spring (March 2025 release: tryouts and interviews in April, training before June).

name: Teen Job and Volunteer Fair (Santa Barbara Public Library)
what_you_do: Meet local employers and nonprofits face to face to find summer jobs, internships and volunteer roles. A teen interview skills workshop is held the following week.
pay_detail: Free to attend.
duration: One afternoon, 2 hours
deadline_text: 2026 fair: Wednesday, April 15, 2026, 4:00 to 6:00 PM at Central Library (workshop April 22). The 2027 date is not posted; the library calls it annual.

grades: Book reviews: grades 7-12. Teen Advisory Board: high school students.
name: Teen Volunteering and Teen Advisory Board (Santa Barbara Public Library)
what_you_do: Earn community service hours at the library through Teen Volunteer Time, the Teen Advisory Board (plan teen programs and shape the collection), or by writing book reviews.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours (1 hour per book review, up to 5 reviews a month).
duration: Teen Volunteer Time: Thursdays 4:15 PM at Central Library (or Saturdays 11 AM to 12:30 PM at Eastside Library). Advisory Board: twice a month on Tuesdays, 5-6:30 PM, during the school year and once a month during the summer.
deadline_text: Teen Advisory Board applications are taken at the start of each school term. Teen Volunteer Time and book reviews are ongoing.

name: Teens Teach Tech (Santa Barbara Public Library)
what_you_do: Learn robotics and coding, then work in pairs to plan and lead one robotics program for children and one for teens at the library (six programs in all).
pay_detail: Unpaid. About 52 community service hours in total.
duration: November 2026 to June 2027, about 2 hours a week (schedule to be set)
deadline_text: Apply by Saturday, October 24, 2026.

name: Dual Enrollment (Santa Barbara City College)
what_you_do: Take real college courses while still in high school, either at your high school (Santa Barbara and Carpinteria Unified students only) or on the SBCC campus or online (all high school and home school students).
pay_detail: Applying to SBCC is free. High-school-based courses cost nothing. For online and campus courses, enrollment fees are waived but students pay student fees and textbooks.
duration: By semester
deadline_text: Fall 2026 dual enrollment registration began July 1. Deadlines for each term are on the Dual Enrollment calendar on the SBCC page.

name: Sea Center Volunteers (Ty Warner Sea Center)
org: Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History, Ty Warner Sea Center
what_you_do: Help guests at the Stearns Wharf aquarium meet live animals, from sea anemones to small sharks, with hands-on demonstrations and live animal talks. Teens 14 and up can train as aquarist volunteers.
pay_detail: Unpaid. A $45 program fee covers uniform, badge and administration; email scvolunteer@sbnature2.org for a fee waiver before your first training.
duration: One shift per week for at least 4 months
deadline_text: The Museum's teen page says the Sea Center accepts volunteer applications year-round.

grades: 10th or 11th grade (outstanding 9th graders considered case by case)
name: Research Mentorship Program (UCSB Summer Sessions)
what_you_do: Do a college-level research project with a mentor (a grad student, postdoc or faculty member), attend a research talk series, and take part in university life for about seven weeks.
pay_detail: 2026 cost page (the 2027 price is not posted): commuter $5,675 total ($75 application fee + $1,000 deposit + $5,600 tuition and program fees); residential $13,274 total (adds $7,599 housing and meals). A limited number of need-based scholarships exist, with priority for California residents.
duration: About 7 weeks (June 14 to July 30, 2027).
deadline_text: Application window Dec 15, 2026 to Mar 8, 2027. Reviews start in January and decisions are rolling.

name: Summer Research Academies (UCSB Summer Sessions)
what_you_do: Pick a research track in STEM, humanities or social sciences, take a 4-unit university course, develop a research topic with an instructor, and present your findings at a capstone seminar.
pay_detail: 2026 cost page (the 2027 price is not posted): commuter $3,475 total ($75 application fee + $900 deposit + $3,400 tuition and program fees); residential $9,874 total (adds $6,399 housing and meals). A limited number of need-based scholarships exist, with priority for California residents.
duration: About 4 weeks (June 25 to July 23, 2027).
deadline_text: Application window Dec 15, 2026 to Mar 22, 2027. Reviews start in January and decisions are rolling.

name: Santa Barbara Youth Council
what_you_do: Speak for teens to City Council and city departments, recommend youth programs and policies, and plan teen events. Meets twice a month.
pay_detail: Unpaid (the City lists compensation as none).
duration: Two-year term, July 1 to June 30. Meets the 1st and 3rd Monday at 5:15 PM at Franklin Neighborhood Center (monthly in July and August).
deadline_text: Fall 2026 City advisory group recruitment: applications due Monday, October 19, 2026 at 5:00 PM. Applications are accepted year-round for future rounds.

name: Santa Barbara Zoo Jobs for Teens (Guest Experience Specialist and seasonal)
what_you_do: Entry-level seasonal jobs such as Guest Experience Specialist and Zoo Camp positions. The Zoo says most openings are for applicants 14 and older and it welcomes first-time workers for entry-level roles.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page; see each job listing.
duration: Seasonal, mostly spring and summer
deadline_text: No dates posted. The Zoo says the busiest hiring is a month before spring and summer school breaks.

name: Zoo Teen Volunteers (Junior Camp Counselor, Leader in Training, Teen Conservation Club)
what_you_do: Help run Zoo Camp as a Junior Camp Counselor or Leader in Training, or join the Teen Conservation Club for monthly meetings and conservation projects.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours.
duration: Junior Camp Counselor: 7 hours a day, Mon-Fri, 3 summer weeks plus 1 fall week and 2 winter weeks
deadline_text: No application dates are posted. The Zoo volunteer page says it is not taking new volunteer recruitment applications at this time (that line sits in the adult sign-up steps), yet the teen sections still show application links. The Leader in Training dates (June 17 to Aug 23) have no year.

name: Santa Clara County Teen CERT Academy
what_you_do: You take a weekend emergency response course on fire safety, search and rescue, stop the bleed and disaster psychology. After it, you can help your community in disasters and earn 20+ volunteer hours.
pay_detail: Free
duration: 3 day academy (Friday evening to Sunday)
deadline_text: Join the waitlist for the next academy. The site shows January 8 to 10 with no year printed. The last academy was March 13 to 15, 2026.

duration: September to May, up to six years
name: Santa Clara Youth Commission
what_you_do: You advise the City Council on issues that affect teens and help plan events like a 5K run. Fifteen teens serve, and the group meets monthly during the school year.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 recruitment is closed. The page does not give 2027-28 dates.

name: County of Santa Clara Intern and Earn
org: County of Santa Clara Employment Connection
what_you_do: You get an eight week paid county internship, plus job-readiness workshops, hiring events and coaching from an Employment Counselor. You work up to 30 hours a week.
pay_detail: $19.75 per hour, up to 30 hours per week
duration: 8 weeks per cohort
deadline_text: Posted 2026 cohorts: Summer deadline May 20, program June 29 to Aug 7. Fall deadline Sept 19, program Oct 19 to Dec 11. The page also says it is accepting applications now; call to ask about the next cohort. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteers (tutor a K-6 student)
what_you_do: Teens 14 and older can volunteer with the Santa Clara County Library District, including tutoring a kindergarten to grade 6 student after school.
deadline_text: Ongoing. No deadline posted.

name: County of Santa Clara Student Internship Program (Level I, high school)
org: County of Santa Clara Employee Services Agency
what_you_do: High school students can work as paid student interns in county departments, helping professional staff under close supervision. Tasks depend on the department.
grades: High school (regular, vocational or working toward equivalency)
pay_detail: Paid on a five-step county salary scale; the rate is not stated on the page (see the county salary plan).
deadline_text: No current posting for Level I. Subscribe to email alerts on the Student Intern, Level I job title or contact county departments. Applications are reviewed as departments ask and expire after 6 months.

name: Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteer Tutor
city: Campbell, Cupertino, Gilroy, Los Altos, Milpitas, Morgan Hill and Saratoga, CA
what_you_do: Teens tutor kindergarten to grade 6 students with homework help after school at a library. You can earn community service hours.
duration: One semester
deadline_text: Ongoing. No deadline posted.

name: Student Advisory Trustee, Schaumburg Township District Library
what_you_do: A non-voting seat on the Library Board. You give feedback on teen programs, speak for teens at Schaumburg, Conant and Hoffman Estates High Schools, attend monthly Board meetings and help with at least two library events.
pay_detail: Not stated
duration: One year: October 2026 to September 2027
deadline_text: The 2026-27 term closed Aug 9, 2026. A new application period is likely in summer 2027 but has not been posted.

name: Sacramento County Office of Education Career Technical Education
what_you_do: Through the Sacramento County Office of Education, you can take career technical education courses in 15 industry sectors. The courses mix technical training with academics. The course catalog is posted online.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.
deadline_text: Course catalog online; no student deadline posted on the page.

name: Volunteer Program (ages 15 and up)
city: San Diego County, CA (La Jolla, Encinitas, San Diego, Chula Vista)
what_you_do: Volunteer at a Scripps hospital in a regular weekly shift in patient and visitor support roles. Open to teens 15 and older.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: At least 6 months and 100 service hours; 2 to 4 hours a week depending on age and position
deadline_text: South region (Scripps Mercy San Diego and Chula Vista): reviewed on an ongoing basis. North region (Scripps Memorial La Jolla and Encinitas, Scripps Green): applications open the first business day of April (May orientation) and of October (November orientation); applications sent outside those periods are not reviewed.

name: Santa Clara Valley Medical Center Volunteers
what_you_do: You staff the hospital information desks or the volunteer office for your first 100 hours, then move to an area you are interested in. After 6 months and 100 hours you can ask about shadowing.
duration: At least 6 months and 100 hours
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Applications are accepted online year-round, and the office is looking for weekday morning or afternoon shifts.

name: Teen Council
what_you_do: Work with museum staff and other teens to share ideas, shape community programs and plan a hands-on art-making workshop. Meets monthly.
pay_detail: No stipend or fee stated on the page.
duration: October 2026 to end of June 2027; monthly meetings on Zoom with several in-person events
deadline_text: 2026-2027 application closed Oct 1, 2026 and the first meeting is Oct 14, 2026. Next year's dates are not posted; expect a similar fall cycle.

grades: 9 to 12 (high school, Running Start, GED or homeschool)
name: Youth Ocean Advocates
what_you_do: Teen volunteers teach visitors about marine life and ocean protection, join conservation projects like beach cleanups and community science, and get behind-the-scenes tours and about 20 hours of training.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program. The page does not mention a cost.
duration: One school year or one summer; at least 8 activities of about 3 to 5 hours each; can stay until the summer after senior year
deadline_text: School Year 2026-27 Currents interest form is closed. The page says to check back in February 2027 for the Summer 2027 interest form (its general timeline says January; confirm with the Aquarium). Info sessions run over Zoom in March (summer) and September (school year).

name: Seattle Children's Hospital Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Weekly volunteer shifts at the hospital and regional clinics. Roles vary; see the position summaries on the volunteer site.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get a badge and free on-site parking.
duration: Most shifts are 3 hours on the same day and time every week; at least 6 months in a row (check each role)
deadline_text: Applications open each March, July and November and stay open until positions are filled. The site lists the next open date (not read).

grades: Entering senior year (the page also says 'between 11th and 12th grade')
name: Fred Hutch Summer High School Internship Program (SHIP)
what_you_do: Eight weeks of paid, full-time lab work: two weeks of lab safety and technique training, then six weeks in a Fred Hutch research group with seminars and college and career workshops, ending in a presentation.
pay_detail: Paid internship; the amount is not stated on the page.
duration: 8 weeks full time (2026: June 22 to Aug 14)
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. The page says information on the 2027 program will be posted in November 2026.

name: Seattle Parks and Recreation Lifeguard
what_you_do: Watch swimmers, respond to emergencies and help teach swim skills at city swim beaches and indoor and outdoor pools.
pay_detail: Listed on the Parks summer jobs page as 'starts at $26.92' (the unit is not stated on the page).
duration: Summer-only at beaches and outdoor pools, or year-round at indoor pools
deadline_text: The last posting closed June 16, 2026. The Aquatics page says Temporary/Intermittent Lifeguards are hired year-round, even when no posting is active.

name: Seattle Parks Youth Employment and Service Learning: Pre-Employment Training
what_you_do: A 7-week, 14-hour after-school job readiness class (resume writing, time management, professional communication) at Teen Life Centers or community centers. Finishing it unlocks Parks paid internships.
pay_detail: After finishing the training you may earn a $300 stipend or Service Learning credit toward high school graduation. Internship pay is not stated on the page.
duration: 7 weeks, 14 hours total, offered each Fall, Winter and Spring quarter
deadline_text: Offered each Fall, Winter and Spring quarter. The page does not list current dates, so email to ask.

grades: Washington high school students in 10th or 11th grade when applying (rising juniors and seniors)
name: Changemakers in Computing
org: University of Washington Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering
what_you_do: A four-week in-person summer program at UW Seattle where students learn coding through projects, explore how technology affects society, and work in groups led by UW undergraduate mentors.
pay_detail: Free. Every mentee gets a $1,200 stipend; lunch and materials are provided. No housing, and bus passes are not provided.
duration: 4 weeks, Monday to Thursday, about 9am to 3pm (2026: July 6 to 30)
deadline_text: 2026 cohort: applications opened March 4 and closed April 1, 2026 (11:59pm PT); decisions April 27; orientation May 16. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Business and Leadership Program (UW Foster School of Business)
org: University of Washington Foster School of Business with Summer Springboard
what_you_do: A two-week summer program on the UW Seattle campus with leadership workshops, a real-world business case competition, and visits to two Seattle companies.
pay_detail: Commuter tuition $4,498 (lunch, a course, excursions, 9am to 5pm Monday to Friday). Residential adds $3,000. Commuters can join weekend excursions for $125 per day. Financial aid is not mentioned on the page.
duration: 2 weeks (2026 session: July 5 to 17)
deadline_text: No deadline stated; 'spaces are limited.' The only session listed was July 5 to 17, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.

grades: Entering 10th to 12th grade in the fall of the program year (2026 page)
name: Woodland Park Zoo Teen Ambassador Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Weekly cohort meetings on conservation careers, public speaking and teamwork, plus 20 self-scheduled volunteer shifts at the zoo, including Zoomazium, new habitats and animal behavior observation.
pay_detail: Active teen volunteers receive a $300 summer stipend to help with transportation, lunches and shoes. No participation fee is listed.
duration: June to September: orientation day, at least 7 of 10 Wednesday meetings (3:30 to 6:30 pm), 20 volunteer hours between June 29 and Sept 6 (2026 dates)
deadline_text: 2026 cohort: application deadline Friday, March 27, 2026, 5:00 pm; Q&A sessions in March; interviews mid-April; decisions early May. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Seattle Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
org: City of Seattle Human Services Department
what_you_do: Paid summer internships in City departments, local businesses and nonprofits (July 6 to Aug 18 in 2026), plus a school-year Learn & Earn job skills program with stipends.
pay_detail: Internship: at least Seattle's minimum wage, listed as $21.30 per hour. Learn & Earn Foundations: $325 stipend at the end of each module. Pathways: monthly stipend, amount not stated.
duration: Internship about 6 weeks (July 6 to Aug 18, 2026). Foundations: October 2026 to March 2027 (tentative), 2-hour weekly sessions.
deadline_text: 2026 internship applications ran March 18 to May 5, 2026 (closed). Learn & Earn Foundations 2026-27 applications ran Aug 11 to Sept 25, 2026 (closed). 2027 dates are not posted.

name: 826 Valencia Youth Programs
what_you_do: You can get free after-school writing help, workshops, summer programs, and college and leadership support. SFPL lists leadership and writing roles for grades 8 to 12 that pay a stipend.
grades: Programs for ages 6 to 18; stipended roles for grades 8 to 12
pay_detail: Free programs; some leadership roles are stipended (amounts not posted)
duration: Varies
deadline_text: No dates posted. Check the 826 Valencia program calendar.

name: Breakthrough Leadership Program (BLP)
what_you_do: High school students serve as role models for middle schoolers in a summer program: co-teach an elective like dance or soccer, help with after-school tutoring, lead cheers and plan events.
pay_detail: Paid through San Francisco's Opportunities for All program (rate not posted on the page). Some hours also count toward school volunteer requirements.
duration: Summer 2026 ran orientation June 15 to 18, then June 22 to July 31, 2026, about 6 weeks
deadline_text: The summer 2026 application is closed. The page says the summer 2027 application launches in early 2027; exact dates not posted.

name: Careers in Science (CiS) Intern Program
what_you_do: You do a paid, year-round internship that lasts 2 to 3 years. You do fieldwork, teach visitors and join research projects after school and on Saturdays.
pay_detail: Paid above minimum wage (rate not posted)
duration: 2 to 3 years through graduation
deadline_text: Applications are closed. The page says to check back in February 2027; closing date not posted.

name: CCSF Dual Enrollment (free college classes)
org: City College of San Francisco and SFUSD
what_you_do: Take free City College classes while in high school and earn both high school and college credit.
pay_detail: Free
duration: By semester
deadline_text: Not stated on the page. Ask your counselor before each term.

name: Community Youth Center Youth Job Fair
org: Community Youth Center of San Francisco
what_you_do: You can attend this one-day job fair. You meet employers, learn about openings, get resume help, practice interviews, take headshots and get free professional clothing.
pay_detail: Free event
duration: Wed Oct 14, 2026, 12 to 4 p.m.
deadline_text: Wednesday, October 14, 2026, 12:00 to 4:00 p.m. at Stonestown Galleria.

name: High School Elections Ambassador Program
what_you_do: Learn how to plan and run pre-registration events that help 16 and 17 year olds sign up to vote. Includes an in-person training and a mentor from the Department of Elections.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Ambassadors get a participation certificate signed by the Mayor and community service hours.
duration: About 2 weeks: Sept 14 to 27 in fall 2026, plus a 90 minute in-person training
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications are closed (the round ran Sept 14 to 27, 2026). The program runs twice a year, in April and September. Spring 2027 dates are not posted.

name: High School Explainer Program
what_you_do: You do a paid museum job. You help visitors at exhibits, lead demonstrations such as cow's eye dissections, and help run museum operations. You get more than 60 hours of training.
pay_detail: Paid job; the wage is not on the program page
duration: A summer session or a school-year session, with over 60 hours of training (20 before working with visitors)
deadline_text: School-year applications are typically posted in July and summer applications in March. Closing dates are not stated.

name: San Francisco Fire Youth Academy
what_you_do: You take a free Saturday program that teaches basic firefighting, CPR and first aid, plus life skills like financial literacy, leadership and time management.
pay_detail: Free to join. Cadets get breakfast, lunch and a bi-weekly stipend (amount not stated).
duration: Saturdays 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., following the SFUSD calendar. A 2025 news article said 15 weeks each fall.
deadline_text: Not stated on the academy's site. A 2025 news article reported an Aug 11, 2025 deadline for the fall class.

name: Girls on the Run Bay Area Junior Coach
org: Girls on the Run Bay Area
what_you_do: Coach elementary and middle school girls in a running and life-skills program as a junior coach, 1.5 to 3 hours a week for 8 to 10 weeks.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 8 to 10 weeks, 1.5 to 3 hours per week; season starts early September, 5K on Nov 14, 2026
